note: Idiom manifest for INDIRECT calls in C -- the ones a name-based resolver drops silently. Declarative data the front-end consumes to classify a call whose callee is not a direct function name: resolve it by idiom where the shape is known, else mark it 'unresolved' and expose it to the engine as a first-class node. A dropped edge is a blind taint/bound path; this makes the blindness explicit and countable.

member_dispatch.describe: x->field(...) / x.field(...) -- a call through a struct member function pointer. Conservatively resolvable to the functions bound to that field elsewhere in the tree; the field name is the idiom key.

unresolvable.describe: fp(...) through a bare function-pointer variable, or tbl[i](...) through a function-pointer array, with no catalogued binding. Mark unresolved; never drop.
